newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs flat in thin, listless trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs flat in thin, listless trade.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures traded listlessly in a shortened session on Thursday as a lack of fresh leads and the absence of players on the eve of Chinese New Year hampered participation.
Dealers said the Nikkei's fall on continued worries about Japan's banking sector and the dollar rally towards 124 yen failed to nudge the market out of its apathetic state.
September Euroyen ended at 99.37 against its IMM close at 99.36. December was steady at 99.24. Turnover for both months was a thin 3,672 lots.
March JGBs remained below the key 126.41 level after Wednesday's rally, settling at 126.10 against a previous 126.33.
"The dollar's strength didn't have any immediate impact on the Nikkei and it failed to filter through to treasuries," said a trader with a U.S. house.
"People are waiting to see what might be said at the G7 meeting this weekend," he said, referring to a meeting of finance ministers from the Group of Seven industrialised nations.
Recent conflicting comments by Japanese and other officials have led to some expectations the G7 might issue a statement on the dollar's current strength.
Eurodollar futures were also trapped in a one-tick band after the Federal Reserve left U.S. interest rates unchanged at its policy-setting meeting on Wednesday.
Dealers said players had shifted their focus to the non-farm payrolls report for January, due on Friday. Estimates for the figure ranged widely from 100,000 to 400,000.
"The labour market seems pretty tight but this close to the Fed leaving rates unchanged, it would take a pretty strong number to trigger a sell-off (in treasuries)," said the trader.
